import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 564

*Reference:* [erdosproblems.com/564](https://www.erdosproblems.com/564)
-/

namespace Erdos564

open Combinatorics Real Filter

/--
Let $R_3(n)$ be the minimal $m$ such that if the edges of the $3$-uniform hypergraph on $m$
vertices are $2$-coloured then there is a monochromatic copy of the complete $3$-uniform
hypergraph on $n$ vertices.

Is there some constant $c>0$ such that
$$ R_3(n) \geq 2^{2^{cn}}? $$
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5]
theorem erdos_564 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop, (2 : ℝ)^(2 : ℝ)^(c * n) ≤ hypergraphRamsey 3 n := by
  sorry

end Erdos564

findings.description: On line 38, Lean infers `c : ℕ`, not `c : ℝ`; `#check` with `pp.all` confirms `@Exists Nat`. Consequently, `c > 0` forces `c ≥ 1`, and the right-hand side is equivalent to `∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, (2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) ^ n) ≤ hypergraphRamsey 3 n`. This equivalence was proved in Lean. The source asks for some positive real constant, allowed to be smaller than 1. Restricting the constant to positive naturals changes the question and is incompatible with the upper bound `R₃(n) < 2^(2^n)` recorded by the cited source. Discarding finitely many small inputs does not fix this restriction.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/564 asks: “Is there some constant $c>0$ such that $R_3(n) \geq 2^{2^{cn}}$?” The following remark records `$2^{cn^2}<R_3(n)<2^{2^n}$` for some constant `$c>0$`. The linked UCSD problem collection, https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~erdosproblems/erdos/newproblems/ThreeHypergraphRamsey.html, likewise asks for an absolute positive constant in `log log r₃(n,n) ≥ cn`.
findings.suggested_fix:
Explicitly type both the constant and the index:
```
theorem erdos_564 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ᶠ (n : ℕ) in atTop,
      (2 : ℝ) ^ ((2 : ℝ) ^ (c * (n : ℝ))) ≤
        (hypergraphRamsey 3 n : ℝ) := by
  sorry
```
Annotating `n` is important: annotating only `c` can instead cause `n` to be inferred as real.

reformulations.difference: The imported helper colours all finite subsets of `Fin m`, rather than only the r-element subsets that are hypergraph edges.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Only colours of subsets with cardinality r are inspected. Restricting an all-subsets colouring therefore gives an edge-colouring; conversely, extend any edge-colouring by assigning `false` to subsets of other cardinalities. These operations preserve the monochromatic-subset condition, so the admissible m and their minimum agree. The colouring-predicate equivalence was proved for arbitrary r, n, and m in /workspace/review/boundaries.lean.

sources_consulted: https://www.erdosproblems.com/564 (read through https://r.jina.ai/https://www.erdosproblems.com/564 after direct access was blocked)
review.notes: The source still marks Problem 564 OPEN, matching the category. The answer placeholder is correctly scoped, and the eventual quantifier appropriately expresses the asymptotic bound. Boundary proofs and finite `decide` tests confirm R₃(n)=n for n=0,1,2,3. In /workspace/review/type_issue.lean, sorry-free proofs additionally show that the natural-valued sequence f(n)=2^(2^(n/2)), using natural division, satisfies the real-constant bound with c=1/4 eventually but satisfies no positive-natural-constant bound. Both experiment files compile. The EHR65 PDF yielded no readable text through the reader; the explicit problem statement and remarks were available from the two problem websites. The reviewed file still matches the requested commit; all experiments were confined to /workspace/review/.

submission.summary: Forced the coefficient c to be real by typing its positivity bound, and explicitly kept the index n natural. The elaborated type confirms the intended real-valued double exponential. The required compile command succeeds with only the expected `declaration uses 'sorry'` warning.
